-- A DOCUMENTED OVERCLAIM, ALSO CORRECTED IN THE DOCS --
REMOVAL.md §1 said "Every client guard is one if on that boolean
[activePresenceMonitoringArmed]". That is not true of the interviewer side, and
the consequence is user-visible, so it is recorded here rather than silently
changed: GreenRoomViewModel.showsPresenceControls is "role == .hostInterview"
and does not consult the server (it cannot — /room/create returns no presence
block). So with the master flag OFF a hiring interviewer still sees the "Record
presence events" checkbox, and ticking it sets activePresenceMonitoringRequested
-> activePresenceSurfaceVisible true -> the interviewer chip and the 15 s poll
start. What they then see is TRUE and nothing is recorded: the poll's
GET /presence/timeline returns 404 PRESENCE_DISABLED so the panel reads "Could
not read the presence timeline.", monitoringEnabled stays false so the chip
reads "Presence monitoring off", no presence* field reaches the room hash, the
candidate's join response carries no presence block, the candidate sees the
legacy alert, and the detector never starts because
activePresenceMonitoringGranted is only ever written by the consent screen the
candidate never reaches. So the zero-impact guarantee is EXACT for the
candidate, the server and the database, and for the interviewer it is "the
surface may appear and it tells the truth". Hiding that checkbox would need a
server capability probe, which would change what the interviewer sees — a
product decision, deliberately NOT made here. Both documents now state this
plainly (design note §2.3, REMOVAL.md §1).
